blocks.text: Anna's behavior is most likely when adult attention is unavailable or directed elsewhere.

items: Prompting appropriate ways to ask for attention or help.
Minimizing attention to concern behavior when safe.
Calmly returning Anna to the replacement response.

blocks.label: Plan focus
blocks.text: Make appropriate attention-seeking easier and more effective than concern behavior.

blocks.label: Safety
blocks.text: Mission: Reinforceable does not add crisis procedures that are not in Anna's plan. Immediate safety concerns should be handled according to existing school procedures; this BIP Map focuses on Anna's plan-supported prevention, teaching, reinforcement, and recovery responses.
Anna's behavior is most likely when adult attention is unavailable.
The behavior may function to bring adult interaction back to Anna.
The implementation goal is not simply to stop behavior; it is to make appropriate attention-seeking more efficient and successful.

items: Arrange engaging independent activities when adult attention will be elsewhere.
Give advance reminders before adult attention shifts away.
Create predictable opportunities for Anna to receive positive adult interaction before concern behavior occurs.

blocks.text: Non-contingent attention is delivered proactively and is not dependent on concern behavior or a replacement request.

items: Use a calm body and voice.
Take a deep breath when prompted or appropriate.

blocks.text: Prompt or model the replacement response early rather than waiting for behavior to escalate. Anna does not need to use every replacement response in every situation.
Immediately reinforce appropriate replacement responding with:

items: Other plan-identified preferred reinforcers when appropriate.

blocks.label: Reinforce quickly
blocks.text: The replacement behavior should contact reinforcement quickly.
Praise should clearly name what Anna did successfully.

items: Minimize or withhold adult attention for concern behavior as described in the BIP.
Promptly cue the appropriate replacement response.
Provide attention or reinforcement when Anna uses the replacement response.
Return to the classroom routine without adding unnecessary attention to the concern behavior.

blocks.label: When safe
blocks.text: Planned ignoring or minimizing attention applies only when safe and consistent with the BIP.

items.definition: Why a behavior is effective for the student or what outcome it tends to produce.
Adult attention delivered proactively on a planned basis, not dependent on concern behavior or a replacement response.
A safer, more appropriate behavior that allows the student to access the same or similar outcome.
A consequence that makes a behavior more likely in the future.
A cue or model that helps the student use the expected replacement response.
Reducing attention following concern behavior when safe and when specifically included in the behavior plan, while continuing to monitor safety and prompt the appropriate replacement behavior.

blocks.text: Mission: Reinforceable data may help the coach notice areas to discuss within normal coaching-as-usual, but the game does not replace the coach's professional judgment.
These are the plan-aligned implementation actions practiced throughout Mission: Reinforceable:

items: Ignore/minimize attention for concern behavior when safe and consistent with the BIP.

blocks.text: Game score is not classroom fidelity.

blocks.label: Practice and measurement
blocks.text: Game practice helps rehearse the plan. Classroom observation is the study's measure of implementation fidelity.
